definition: Reddish brown, especially the warm brown of autumn leaves, weathered leather, or certain apples and pears; also, a coarse homespun cloth of that color.
etymology: It came through Old French rousset, meaning “reddish,” a diminutive of rous. Behind it is Latin russus, “red”: a small red word that mellowed, in English, into October brown.
usage: By October 19, the beeches had begun to turn russet along the lane.
